evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We run monthly immunization camps in 40 villages of Udaipur district, Rajasthan. Behavior: mothers of children aged 9 to 12 months in Kherwara block bring the child to the camp for the measles dose on camp day. Camp registers show 68% of eligible children in the block got the dose last quarter. We interviewed 200 mothers: they believe only about 4 in 10 neighbors bring their child, and most say a mother who vaccinates is doing the right thing. Channel: the ASHA (village health worker) reads a card aloud at the household visit the week before camp day, in Hindi; the card is signed by the block medical officer. We can see from the register which households vaccinated last round. Write the norm message.
evals.expected_output: A social norm message in the output template that states the 68% figure for mothers in Kherwara block without rounding it up.
assertions: States the belief the message corrects: about 4 in 10 believed against 68% in the registers.
The message gives the share as 6 out of 10, more than 6 out of 10, or 68 of every 100, and not 7 out of 10.
The group named in the message is the group the register figure describes.
The message contains a line of approval for mothers who already vaccinated.
No line says how many mothers did not vaccinate.
Sets a comparison that follows households that vaccinated last round separately, and promises no effect size.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: People in our program aren't paying their water bills on time. Write a norm message.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks what customers believe others do and what share really pays on time, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks what share of a named group pays on time, with the source and date.
Asks what customers believe other customers do or approve of, and how that was learned.
Does not use the word "most" about customers who pay.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: HIV self-testing in Lagos: our clinic records and a household survey show that 31% of men aged 18 to 35 in the Mushin catchment have ever taken an HIV self-test. In the survey most of them said testing is something other men do not do and would be judged for. We want to send an SMS from the clinic saying 'most men like you have already tested' to push the rest. Can you write it?
evals.expected_output: The skill declines to write that message because 31% is not most men, and names the specialists who must review any message on a stigmatized behavior.
assertions: Says "most men like you have already tested" would be false at 31%.
Does not widen the group or change the figure to make the claim true.
Says no approval message can be written because the share of men who approve was not measured, or that the survey suggests they do not.
Names a local qualitative researcher and a safeguarding lead, or a behavioral scientist, as the specialist.
Says what to bring to them.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Our water utility in Nakuru wants to print a box on every household's monthly bill showing how many liters that household used next to the average for its street. Can you write the norm message for the box?
evals.expected_output: The skill says a report comparing each household with its neighbors is a different design and points to the skill for it.
assertions: Says this is a comparison of each household's own record with its peers', not one message about what most people do.
Does not write a message or fill the output template.
